response.justification: The candidate is an experienced generalist software engineer (13+ years) with strong web, backend, and full-stack credentials, but the resume shows essentially none of the core requirements for a Principal Performance Architect role in AI accelerator silicon. There is no SoC/IP modeling, RTL or architectural simulation, GPU/SIMD/MIMD architecture, deep-learning training/inference optimization, or hardware-software co-design experience. The closest adjacent work is low-latency service engineering in D at Sociomantic, some C/C++ at National Instruments, and a wave-field-synthesis audio thesis — all far removed from AI accelerator microarchitecture. Education (BS in CS) meets the 8+ years bar in years only, not in domain relevance.
strengths: 13+ years of broad software engineering across web, mobile, desktop, and embedded
Demonstrated low-latency, high-throughput systems work (millions of req/s, async I/O, caching)
Strong engineering discipline: TDD, CI/CD, open-source tooling, public speaking and teaching
concerns: No SoC/IP modeling, hardware architecture, or silicon design experience
No AI/deep-learning workload, GPU, or SIMD/MIMD accelerator background
Career trajectory is application/web-focused, not principal-level hardware performance architecture

key_factors.factor: Missing SoC/IP modeling and hardware architecture experience
No AI accelerator / DNN optimization or GPU workload analysis
Long tenure and low-latency systems performance work
